hypotheses.description: Candidate mechanisms for the observed behavior. Do not pick a winner; the caller runs the checks.

id.description: Short unique id such as H1, used to refer to this item later.

mechanism.description: Which code does what, under which condition, to produce the observed behavior.

evidence_for.description: What in the code or material supports it.

evidence_against.description: What in the code or material argues against it.

predicts.description: What this hypothesis predicts that the others do not.

discriminating_check.description: A command or observation whose result differs depending on whether this hypothesis is true.

basis.description: traced: followed the code path by reading it; ran: executed a command that shows it; inferred: reasoning without either.

no_bug_found.description: If the observed behavior is expected or correct, explain why; otherwise null.

would_change_my_mind.description: Evidence that would change your verdict. Empty if none.

need.description: The fact or result you would need to see.

why.description: How it would change your verdict.

questions_for_user.description: Questions only the user can answer, such as how to reproduce, environment details or facts outside the code. Empty if none.

recommended.description: The answer you expect or would pick, and why.

caller_challenge.description: Set only when you disagree with a direction the caller has already chosen; otherwise null.

challenge.description: What you think is wrong with the chosen direction.

context_possibly_missing.description: Context the caller may have that you do not, which would make this challenge wrong.

cost_if_wrong.description: What it costs if the caller follows this challenge and you are wrong.

summary.description: 1-3 sentences. No praise, no restating the material.

verdict.description: found: the code already rules out every other hypothesis; need_data: the discriminating checks have to be run first; no_bug: the behavior is expected.
